findings.title: Cache is not re-checked after acquiring the write lock
findings.body: After the read-lock fast path misses, the function takes the write lock and unconditionally re-reads/re-parses the manifest (readWebAssetsFromFile) and republishes the cache, without re-checking entryPointAssetsCache. On a cold start, N goroutines can all observe the cache as nil under RLock, then serialize on the write lock and each perform a full file open + JSON decode of assets-manifest.json even though the first one already populated the cache. The consequence is redundant sequential I/O and CPU per waiter (a thundering herd) right at startup. Re-check `if entryPointAssetsCache != nil` (for non-dev env) immediately after acquiring the write lock to avoid this.

findings.title: Write lock is held during blocking I/O
findings.body: The exclusive lock (taken at line 48 and held via defer until return) covers the entire manifest read, including readWebAssetsFromFile (file open + JSON decode) and, when the CDN path is enabled, readWebAssetsFromCDN (an HTTP GET with the request context). While the writer holds the lock, all other GetWebAssets callers block on RLock, so slow disk or a slow/hanging CDN response stalls every concurrent request. In dev mode this happens on every call. A better structure is to build the result outside the lock and only hold the write lock briefly to publish it, or use sync.Once for the non-dev path.
